# SB-1031 Safety bulletin: noise exposure

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-SB03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-033, ECN-2026-036, SB-1021

## Hazard description

Operations that produce intermittent high-energy impacts and particulate agitation, such as the shot blast process on Hot Forge shot blast cabinet EQ-P2-L1-SB03, create elevated noise levels in the immediate work area. These noise sources are variable with process state, maintenance condition, and shot media quantity. Prolonged or repeated exposure to elevated noise can cause permanent hearing loss and increased risk of distraction-related incidents during adjacent operations. Secondary hazards include reduced ability to hear warnings and team communications, leading to process deviations and potential mechanical interference with the hot forge workflow.

This bulletin addresses exposure risks specifically associated with the shot blast cabinet EQ-P2-L1-SB03 as configured on line P2-L1. The bulletin clarifies control expectations for operations personnel, maintenance staff, and supervisors to reduce worker exposure and maintain audibility of safety signals.

## Affected equipment

- Hot Forge shot blast cabinet: EQ-P2-L1-SB03 (located on line P2-L1 in plant P2).
- Immediate area adjacent to EQ-P2-L1-SB03 where ingress and egress, staging, and tool handover occur.
- Work positions that rely on direct verbal communication with operators at EQ-P2-L1-SB03 while the cabinet is in service.

Refer to ECN-2026-033 for the recent configuration update to the blast cabinet enclosure and ECN-2026-036 for the installed lining and barrier changes that affect acoustic transmission. SB-1021 contains the corporate hearing conservation program baseline; this bulletin provides equipment-specific actions that align with that program.

## Required controls

Administrative and engineering controls are required to manage noise exposure around EQ-P2-L1-SB03. Controls must be implemented in the following prioritized order.

Engineering controls
- Maintain and verify blast cabinet enclosure integrity per ECN-2026-036. Ensure all access panels and barrier seals are fitted and secured before operation. Replace or re-seal any compromised barrier components identified during pre-shift checks.
- Verify that the shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 33 hours. Do not exceed this top-up interval without documented authorization from maintenance engineering. The top-up interval is linked to cabin damping performance and consistent noise attenuation.
- Ensure mechanical isolation and damping hardware on EQ-P2-L1-SB03 is inspected after any impact or transit event and following any maintenance that requires partial disassembly. Restore all mounts and isolation features to service condition before returning the cabinet to operation.

Administrative controls
- Restrict nonessential personnel from the immediate area during shot blast cycles. Implement clear visual markings and transient-info signage at the perimeter of the blast area to indicate active blast status.
- Define and communicate a process for team communication while the cabinet is active. Use pre-agreed hand signals, clipboard sign-off, or other redundant means that do not rely on unamplified speech.
- Schedule tasks that require close verbal interaction with operators at EQ-P2-L1-SB03 to occur during known low-activity windows, such as when the cabinet is not actively blasting or is isolated for maintenance.

Personal protective equipment
- Provide hearing protection compatible with hot forge PPE requirements and ensure all personnel working adjacent to EQ-P2-L1-SB03 use the devices during all blast operations. Hearing protection must be stored in a clean, accessible location and inspected before use.

Training and supervision
- Incorporate EQ-P2-L1-SB03 specific noise risk and control procedures into operator and maintenance training modules referenced in SB-1021.
- Supervisors must verify control adherence during each shift and document verification as part of the area control log.

Rationale for controls
- The shot media top-up interval of 33 hours for the cabinet is based on observed correlations between media level, cabinet damping, and acoustic emissions following the updates in ECN-2026-036. Maintaining the specified top-up interval supports stable media behavior and consistent acoustic attenuation, reducing variability in worker exposure risk.
- Enclosure integrity and isolation hardware ensure that engineering controls function as designed. Administrative restrictions and communication protocols reduce the probability of miscommunication and exposure during active operations.
- Documented verification and training close the gap between procedure and practice, ensuring personnel can consistently apply required controls.

Examples and scenarios

- Example: An operator prepares the blast cabinet for a scheduled batch. Prior to starting, the operator confirms media top-up is within the required 33 hours and that all access panels are secured. The operator posts an active-blast card at the area entrance and uses the established hand-signal protocol to coordinate part transfer with the forge operator. This sequence prevents unnecessary verbal exposure and maintains area boundary integrity.
- Example: Maintenance completes a lining repair referenced in ECN-2026-036. Before returning EQ-P2-L1-SB03 to service, the maintenance lead verifies mechanical isolation mounts and seals, documents the check, and communicates the status to production supervision. This reduces post-maintenance variability in noise output.

Records to keep

- Area control log entries documenting pre-operation checks of EQ-P2-L1-SB03 enclosure integrity and confirmation of the shot media top-up interval of 33 hours. Logs must reference the responsible operator or maintenance lead and note any deviations from required condition.
- Maintenance records for any work performed on EQ-P2-L1-SB03, including references to ECN-2026-036 where applicable. Records must document isolation hardware inspections and any actions taken to restore damping or seals.
- Training completion records demonstrating that affected personnel have reviewed noise-control procedures specific to EQ-P2-L1-SB03, cross-referenced with SB-1021.

Effective date

Effective date: Upon issuance of Rev B

Distribution and questions

This bulletin is applicable to all personnel assigned to line P2-L1 and maintenance teams supporting EQ-P2-L1-SB03. For clarification or exceptions, contact the plant safety engineer and reference ECN-2026-033, ECN-2026-036, and SB-1021.
